introduction.text: The Mausoleum of Helena is an ancient Roman mausoleum in Rome, built by Emperor Constantine I between 326 and 330 as his own tomb, later dedicated to his mother Saint Helena.

history.description: Construction of the mausoleum by Constantine I between 326 and 330.
Helena's death in 330 and the mausoleum's assignment as her tomb.
In the 8th century the mausoleum was repurposed as a defensive fortress.
In the 11th century the sarcophagus was moved to the Lateran.
The area was used as a cemetery for the Equites singulares.
The mausoleum was damaged by the reuse of its materials for other constructions.

design.description: The mausoleum has a circular plan with two cylindrical sections, the lower octagonal cylinder and the upper smaller diameter cylinder, originally 25.4 m tall.
The lower cylinder is octagonal with niches at the vertices, and the upper ring has eight arcaded windows.
Large amphorae were used to lighten the dome, visible after the vault collapsed.
The mausoleum's height has reduced from 25.4 m to about 18 m.

art.description: The sarcophagus of Helena, made of red porphyry, is decorated with war scenes.
The rectangular niche facing the entrance likely contained the sarcophagus.
